oewn-00008423-r.learner: to a complete degree, or to the full extent.
examples: By morning the snow was all gone.
You have got the story all wrong.

oewn-02494483-v.learner: to take someone as your husband or wife.
examples: But to live with and to marry, I do not know that any one of the four can come into competition with Elizabeth.
he wants nothing but a little more liveliness, and that, if he marry prudently, his wife may teach him

oewn-02495105-v.learner: to carry out the ceremony that makes two people husband and wife.
examples: A local clergyman married the couple in the village church.

Mr. Bennet replied that he had not.

oewn-07505853-n.learner: a basic good feeling that is hard to explain but that people want to have.
examples: I do assure you that the news does not affect me either with pleasure or pain.

oewn-01073670-n.learner: something you do that gives you enjoyment.
examples: The last born has as good a right to the pleasures of youth as the first.
He put his work before his pleasures.

oewn-05838106-n.learner: a thing or a person that is a source of happiness.
examples: Her letters were the greatest pleasure of his week.
The old garden was his one remaining pleasure.

oewn-01231134-n.learner: a polite act that shows you care for someone.
examples: His attentions to Miss King were now the consequence of views solely and hatefully mercenary.
my friend Denny tempted me further by his account of the very great attentions Meryton had procured them

oewn-05710222-n.learner: the way a person fixes the mind on some of the things around them and leaves the rest out.
examples: Her attention drifted from the lecture to the noise in the street.

oewn-05862201-n.learner: broad interest from people that makes them want to know more.
examples: The stranger's arrival drew the attention of the whole village.

oewn-06612141-n.learner: the thing that people are talking about in a conversation or discussion.
examples: On this subject I have nothing more to say, no other apology to offer.

oewn-05822417-n.learner: a situation or event that someone thinks about.
examples: He turned the whole subject over in his mind during the long drive.

oewn-06005806-n.learner: one area of knowledge that people learn and teach.
examples: History was her best subject at school.

oewn-00035445-r.learner: many times, with only short gaps between them.

oewn-00059951-r.learner: many times, or in a large amount.
examples: She thinks of him often.

oewn-00037620-r.learner: in a way that fits the truth, the facts, or what is real.

oewn-00032295-r.learner: used before a word to make it stronger.

oewn-00038407-r.learner: in fact - used to add force to a whole sentence.

oewn-01886163-v.learner: to go out for a walk, for the pleasure of it.

oewn-00019380-r.learner: of a kind that is unusually noticeable, exceptional, or remarkable.
